threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the Blackstock Road bus is the fastest way to get to Finsbury Park. Everyone else just bikes it or walks through the park.
Caught a guy on the 333 last night singing opera to himself. Did a whole aria before the driver told him to pipe down. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a random guy painting a mural on the bus stop while the bus was late, and everyone just sat there, sipping their coffee like it was normal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that doubles as a dance studio on weekends; grab a beer and watch the tango lessons unfold!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A true local rolls their eyes when someone asks for directions to the 'BART station'—it's always 'Civic Center' or 'Powell,' never just 'the BART.'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus trying to barter a sandwich for a single fare. The driver just shook his head, but the whole bus cracked up.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often assume all bars close by 2am, but in Gràcia, the real life starts after midnight—it's when the locals come out to play.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new by their hesitation at the metro turnstiles—always looking for the right way to swipe their T-10.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think every café is just a coffee shop, not realizing half of them serve six types of avocado toast.
Caught a group of teenagers on the N35 singing classic grime tracks, off-key but loud. Their energy lit up the damp night. Brixton never sleeps.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a bus the other day, and the driver gave a whole history lesson about the route. Only in Neukölln do you get your daily dose of local lore with your ride.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Kiez that turns a former tram depot into a pop-up beach club. Sand, cocktails, and a DJ—it's a summer vibe like no other.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they seamlessly switch from English to Spanglish while ordering tacos at La Taqueria without missing a beat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver paused for a street performer—everyone on board started clapping. Only in SF do you jam out on your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the local bars are just for sipping cocktails, but really, we gather over a simple glass of vermut and good conversation.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle to navigate the narrow, winding streets, often stopping to consult maps or smartphones every few minutes.
